To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have presented a new method to calculate the transfer function of PCA and applied it to the AzTEC data to improve the flux density estimates of point sources in AzTEC maps.
the transfer function for principal component analysis (PCA) is dependent upon the instrument and the reduction pipeline used.
the AzTEC flux densities and noise are revised upwards by roughly +10–15 per cent for fields where the array was installed at the CSO and +15–30 per cent for fields at JCMT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique for measuring the transfer functions of principal component analysis, which is a widely used technique for reducing data from instruments with many bolometers.
the development of a new technique for the reduction of data obtained with bolometric array instruments.
the analysis of the transfer functions of principal component analysis for point sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AzTEC data reduction pipeline is now in its best shape ever.
AzTEC is not a perfect instrument, but the data are still very good.
the AzTEC photometric accuracy is better than the previously published estimates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the noise in the AzTEC maps was overestimated by 10–20 per cent.
the noise in the data is underestimated by a factor of 1.2–2.0 and the fluxes are underestimated by 10–25 per cent, depending on the field and observing configuration.
the noise level in the AzTEC maps is not significantly different than previously reported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the noise properties and source flux densities of AzTEC data are not as well understood as previously believed.
the transfer function of PCA is not constant and depends on the spatial distribution of the signal.

, in general, one must take care when using non-linear and iterative reduction methods on data from bolometric arrays, as these techniques may not preserve the statistical properties of the signal of interest.
